biography: Cleiton Krause, a name whispered with anticipation in Brazilian motorsport circles, hails from the sun-drenched favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His journey began not on the polished tarmac, but on the makeshift dirt tracks carved into the hillsides, where he raced battered go-karts cobbled together from scrap. His raw talent was undeniable, a diamond in the rough spotted by a local mechanic who convinced a small racing academy to give him a shot. Cleiton remembers those early days vividly, particularly one sweltering afternoon when, with a blown engine and a burning desire to win, he pushed his kart across the finish line, earning the respect of his peers and a spot on the academy's roster. His steady temperament served him well as he climbed the ranks, catching the eye of Passat Classic FL team owner, Ricardo Oliveira, who saw in Cleiton the potential to revive the team's flagging fortunes. Now, at 27, Cleiton carries the hopes of a nation, striving to prove that talent can bloom even in the most unlikely of environments.
drivingStyle: Cleiton's driving style is characterized by a remarkable blend of calculated aggression and uncanny car control. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers, preferring to meticulously analyze his opponents' weaknesses and exploit them with surgical precision. His tire management is exceptional, often allowing him to maintain a consistent pace throughout a stint while others fade. Under pressure, Cleiton remains remarkably calm, his heart rate barely registering a blip as he navigates the most intense moments of a race.

rivalries.reason: Esteves, a veteran driver, publicly dismissed Cleiton's talent as 'favela luck,' sparking a fierce on-track rivalry.
Flores and Krause are often neck-and-neck, battling for championship points. A controversial collision at Interlagos fueled the rivalry.
Vargas, known for his aggressive driving, has a history of run-ins with Krause, often resulting in heated exchanges after races.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific samba song before entering his car to center himself.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his racing gloves before each session, regardless of how clean they already are.
famousQuote: "Pressure? Pressure is trying to feed your family when you don't know where the next meal is coming from. This is racing. This is opportunity."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Stock Car Championship in his rookie year, defying all expectations and cementing his status as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Rio de Janeiro Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure, a heartbreaking moment in front of his home crowd.
